newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols subdued before job report.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols subdued before job report.

text.p: Interest rate options implied volatilities showed little change Thursday, holding at relatively low levels for the session before a U.S. employment report, options traders said.
May Treasury bond volatility was quoted late in the day at 9.45 percent, where it also opened, but up 0.2 point from the previous session.
June was pegged at 9.20 percent, up slightly from 9.15 percent at the opening and on Wednesday.

A bond options floor broker said volatilities were exceptionally low given the importance the market has traditionally attached to the monthly jobs data and the mixed expectations for the March report in particular.
According to a Reuters survey, the consensus forecast is for an increase of 196,000 in non-farm payrolls.
"The last employment number, volatility was as low as it's ever been. This time breaks the record," the bond options broker said.
Activity in debt options focused on squaring up positions before the report, with bond traders noted buying puts presumably to hedge downside exposure, floor brokers said.
Eurodollar traders also were seen exiting long volatility positions.
The narrow-range trade in underlying futures also weighed on volatilities in several Eurodollar options months, although nearby June was firm at 8.50 percent.
Volatility was estimated at 11.00 percent in September, 12.50 in December, 13.80 in March, 15.00 in June 1998 and 16.10 in September 1998.
